extraction_notes.note: Definition environments asserting existence of combinators ('There is ... such that'); kept as definition because they introduce the named combinators (Lean defs), though their content is an existence claim (proposition).
Source typos kept verbatim: evaluation clause gives [[S]] = K, and Y's equation mentions Z; Lean \uses/\lean blueprint macros are stripped, so dependencies were inferred from terms.

nodes.name: Partial elements
nodes.statement: The set of \emph{partial elements} $\Part{A}$ in $A$ is \begin{equation*} \Part{A} = \set{ u \subseteq A \such \all{x, y \in u} x = y}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Partial elements of $A$: subsets of $A$ with at most one element.

nodes.name: Total value
nodes.statement: We think of $\emptyset$ as the undefined value and $\set{a}$ the defined, or \emph{total} value $a \in A$.

nodes.name: Definedness of a partial element
nodes.statement: Given $u \in \Part{A}$, write $\defined{u}$ to mean that $u$ is defined, i.e., $\some{a \in A} a \in u$.

nodes.name: Partial elements in the formalization
nodes.statement: Initial experimentation with formalization shows that it is advantageous to work with partial elements rather than elements, as that avoids coercions and helps the rpoof assistant compute types. When a partial element should be total this is expressed as a separate claim.

nodes.name: Partial application
nodes.statement: A \emph{partial application} on a set $A$ is a map ${-} \cdot_A {-} : \Part{A} \times \Part{A} \to \Part{A}$.
nodes.label: def:partial-application

nodes.name: Application notation
nodes.statement: We also write $u \, v$ and $u \cdot v$ in place of $u \cdot_A v$ and we associate application to the left, so that $u \cdot v \cdot w = (u \cdot v) \cdot w$.
nodes.statement_short: Juxtaposition and $\cdot$ denote application, associating to the left.

nodes.name: Non-standard partial application without strictness
nodes.statement: The preceding defintion is non-standard, as one usually expects ${-} \cdot_A {-} : A \times A \to \Part{A}$. However, as explained above, we prefer our definition as it is easier to work with. You might also have expected strictness conditions stating that $\defined{u \cdot_A v}$ implies $\defined{u}$ and $\defined{v}$, which we did have in the initial formalization, but they were never used. It looks like our formalization already lead to a small discovery, namely that partial combinatory algebras work just as well when its elements can be applied to undefined values.
nodes.statement_short: Application on partial elements is non-standard; strictness conditions were never needed, so PCAs work with application to undefined values.

nodes.name: Partial combinatory algebra (PCA)
nodes.statement: A set $A$ with a partial map ${-} \cdot_A {-}$ is a \emph{partial combinatory algebra (PCA)} if there are elements $\combK, \combS \in \Part{A}$ such that, for all $u, v, w \in \Part{A}$: \begin{align*} &\defined{K}, & &\defined{S},\\ &\defined{u} \lthen \defined{\combK \, u}, & &\defined{u} \lthen \defined{\combS \, u}, \\ &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \lthen \defined{\combK \, u \, v}, & &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \lthen \defined{\combS \, u \, v}, \\ &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \lthen \combK \, u \, v = u, & &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \land \defined{w} \lthen \defined{\combS \, u \, v \, w}, \\ && &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \land \defined{w} \lthen \combS \, u \, v \, w = (u \, w) \, (v \, w), \\ \end{align*}
nodes.genus: A set $A$ with a partial map ${-} \cdot_A {-}$
differentia: there are elements $\combK, \combS \in \Part{A}$ such that, for all $u, v, w \in \Part{A}$
nodes.statement_short: A PCA is a set with partial application having defined combinators K and S satisfying definedness and the K, S equations.
nodes.label: def:PCA

nodes.name: Expressions
nodes.statement: Given a set $\Gamma$ of \emph{variables} and a set $A$ of elements, the \emph{expressions} $\Expr \Gamma A$ are generated inductively by the following clauses: \begin{itemize} \item the constants $\mathtt{K}$ and $\mathtt{S}$ are expressions, \item an element $a \in A$ is an expression, \item a variable $x \in \Gamma$ is an expression, \item if $e_1$ and $e_2$ are expressions then $e_1 \cdot e_2$ is an expression. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Expressions over variables $\Gamma$ and elements $A$: constants K, S, elements, variables, and formal application.
nodes.label: def:expression

nodes.name: Formal application in expressions
nodes.statement: The application $e_1 \cdot e_2$ in the third clause of the definition is formal, i.e., it is just a constructor of an inductive datatype. We again deviated from the standard definition in an inessential way by including primitive constants $\combK$ and $\combS$, separate from the corresponding elements of~$A$.

nodes.name: Valuation
nodes.statement: Given a set of variables $\Gamma$ and a set~$A$, a \emph{valuation} is a map $\eta : \Gamma \to A$ which assigns elements to variables.

nodes.name: Override of a valuation
nodes.statement: Given a valuation $\eta : \Gamma \to A$, $x \in A$ and $a \in a$, we may \emph{override} $\eta$ to get a valuation $\override \eta x a : \Gamma \to A$ such that \begin{equation*} (\override \eta x a) y = \begin{cases} \eta(y) &\text{if $y \in \Gamma$,}\\ a &\text{if $y = x$.} \end{cases} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Override valuation $\eta$ at variable $x$ with value $a$.
nodes.label: def:override

nodes.name: Evaluation of an expression
nodes.statement: The \emph{evaluation} $\eval e \eta$ of an expression $e \in \Expr \Gamma A$ in a PCA~$A$ at a valuation $\eta : \Gamma \to A$ is defined recursively by the clauses \begin{align*} \eval{\combK}{\eta} &= \combK \\ \eval{\combS}{\eta} &= \combK \\ \eval{a}{\eta} &= a &&\text{if $a \in A$}\\ \eval{x}{\eta} &= \eta(x) &&\text{if $x \in \Gamma$}\\ \eval{e_1 \cdot e_2}{\eta} &= (\eval{e_1} \eta) \cdot_A (\eval{e_2} \eta). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Recursive evaluation of an expression in a PCA at a valuation, interpreting formal application as $\cdot_A$.
nodes.label: def:evaluation

nodes.name: Defined expression
nodes.statement: An expression $e \in \Expr \Gamma A$ is \emph{defined} when $\defined{\eval{e}{\eta}}$ for all $\eta : \Gamma \to A$.
nodes.label: def:expression-defined

nodes.name: Abstraction
nodes.statement: The \emph{abstraction} of an expression $e \in \Expr \Gamma A$ with respect to a variable $x \in \Gamma$ is the expression $\abstr{x} e \in \Expr \Gamma A$ defined recursively by \begin{align*} \abstr{x} x &= \combS \cdot \combK \cdot \combK, \\ \abstr{x} y &= \combK \cdot y &&\text{if $x \neq y \in \Gamma$}, \\ \abstr{x} a &= \combK \cdot a &&\text{if $a \in A$}, \\ \abstr{x} (e_1 \cdot e_2) &= \combS \cdot (\abstr{x} e_1) \cdot (\abstr{x} e_2). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bracket abstraction $[x]e$ defined recursively via S and K.
nodes.label: def:abstraction

nodes.name: Abstraction is defined
nodes.statement: An abstraction $\abstr{x} e$ is defined.
nodes.label: prop:abstraction-defined

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: By straightforward structural induction on~$e$.
nodes.statement_short: Structural induction on $e$.

nodes.name: Combinatory completeness
nodes.statement: Let $x \in \Gamma$ and $e \in \Expr {(\Gamma \cup \{x\})} A$. Then for every $a \in A$ and $\eta : \Gamma \to A$ \begin{equation*} \eval{(\abstr{x} e) \cdot a}{\eta} = \eval{e}{\override{\eta}{x}{a}}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Applying the abstraction $[x]e$ to $a$ evaluates like $e$ with $x$ set to $a$ (beta rule).
nodes.label: prop:abstraction-equal

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2
nodes.statement: By straightforward structural induction on~$e$.
nodes.statement_short: Structural induction on $e$.

nodes.name: Combinators
nodes.statement: We call the elements of~$A$ accomplishing various programming tasks \emph{combinators}.

nodes.name: Identity combinator
nodes.statement: There is the \emph{identity combinator} $\comb{I} \in A$ such that $I \, a = a$ for all $a \in A$.
nodes.label: def:combinator-I

nodes.name: Pairing combinators
nodes.statement: There are combinators $\comb{pair}, \comb{fst}, \comb{snd} \in A$ such that, for all $a, b \in A$, \begin{align*} \comb{fst}\, (\comb{pair}\,a\,b) &= a, & \comb{snd}\, (\comb{pair}\,a\,b) &= b. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combinators pair, fst, snd with the projection equations.
nodes.label: def:combinator-pairing

nodes.name: Boolean combinators
nodes.statement: There are combinators $\comb{ite} \, \comb{fal}, \comb{tru} \in A$ such that, for all $a, b \in a$, \begin{equation*} \comb{ite} \, \comb{tru} \ ,a \, b = a \text{and} \comb{ite} \, \comb{fal} \, a \, b = b. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Combinators ite, tru, fal implementing if-then-else.
nodes.label: def:combinator-bool

nodes.name: Numerals (Curry numerals with primitive recursion)
nodes.statement:
For each $n \in \NN$ there is $\overline{n} \in A$, as well as combinators $\comb{succ}, \comb{primrec} \in A$ such that, for all $n \in \NN$ and $a, f \in A$,  egin{align*} \comb{succ} \, 
umeral{n} &= 
umeral{n+1}, \ \comb{primrec} \, a \, f \, 
umeral{0} &= a, \ \comb{primrec} \, a \, f \, 
umeral{n+1} &= f \, 
umeral{n} \, (\comb{primrec} \, a \, f \, 
umeral{n}). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Numerals $\overline{n}$ with successor and primitive recursion combinators.
nodes.label: def:combinator-nat

nodes.name: Fixed-point combinator Y
nodes.statement: There is a combinator $\comb{Y} \in A$ such that, for all $a \in A$, \begin{equation*} \comb{Y} \, a = a (\comb{Z} \, a). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Fixed-point combinator Y with $Y a = a(Z a)$.
nodes.label: def:combinator-Y

nodes.name: General recursion combinator Z
nodes.statement: There is a combinator $\comb{Z} \in A$ such that, for all $f, a \in A$, \begin{equation*} \defined{\comb{Z} \, f}, \qquad\text{and}\qquad \comb{Z} \, f \, a = f (\comb{Z} \, f) \, a. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Call-by-value fixed-point combinator Z: $Z f$ defined and $Z f a = f (Z f) a$.
nodes.label: def:combinator-Z

nodes.name: Represented partial map
nodes.statement: A partial map $f : A \parto A$ is \emph{represented} by $a \in A$ when, for all $b \in B$, $f(b) = a \cdot b$.
nodes.label: def:representable-function

nodes.name: Representability of general recursive maps
nodes.statement: Every general recursive map $f : \NN \parto \NN$ is represented in the following sense: there is $a \in A$ such that, for all $n \in \NN$, if $\defined{f(n)}$ then $\numeral{f(n)} = a \cdot \numeral{n}$.
conclusions: there is $a \in A$ such that, for all $n \in \NN$, if $\defined{f(n)}$ then $\numeral{f(n)} = a \cdot \numeral{n}$
nodes.statement_short: Every general recursive partial function on $\NN$ is represented in a PCA on numerals.
nodes.label: thm:recursive-map-representable

nodes.name: (Total) combinatory algebra (CA)
nodes.statement: A \emph{(total) combinatory algebra (CA)} is given by a carrier set $A$ and a \emph{total} binary operation ${-} \cdot {-} : A \times A \to A$, such that there are $\combK, \combS$ satisfying the characteristic equations \begin{equation*} \combK \cdot x \cdot y = x \qquad\text{and}\qquad \combS \cdot x \cdot y \cdot z = (x \cdot z) \cdot (y \cdot z). \end{equation*}
nodes.genus: a carrier set $A$ and a \emph{total} binary operation ${-} \cdot {-} : A \times A \to A$
differentia: there are $\combK, \combS$ satisfying the characteristic equations
nodes.label: def:CA

nodes.name: Every CA is a PCA
nodes.statement: Every combinatory algebra is a partial combinatory algebra.
conclusions: Every combinatory algebra is a partial combinatory algebra.
nodes.label: prop:CAisPCA

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement: Simply reuse the total application as the partial one.
nodes.statement_short: Use the total application as the partial one.

nodes.name: Free combinatory algebra
nodes.statement: The \emph{free combinatory algebra} is generated freely by the symbols $\combK$ and $\combS$ and formal binary application, quotiented by provable equality.
nodes.statement_short: Terms in K, S and application modulo provable equality.
nodes.label: def:FreeCA

nodes.name: Listing
nodes.statement: A \emph{listing} on a set $A$ is a section $\mathsf{fromList} : \mathsf{List}\,A \to A$ and a retraction $\mathsf{toList} : A \to \mathsf{List}\,A$.
nodes.genus: section $\mathsf{fromList} : \mathsf{List}\,A \to A$ and a retraction $\mathsf{toList} : A \to \mathsf{List}\,A$
nodes.label: def:Listing

nodes.name: Pairing induced by a listing
nodes.statement: Suppose $A$ is a set with a listing. It induces a pairing on $A$: $\pair{x, y} = \mathsf{fromList}\,[x,y]$ with corresponding projections.

nodes.name: toSet
nodes.statement: Each $x \in A$ may be seen as a finite subset of $A$, \begin{equation*} \mathsf{toSet}\,x = \set{y \such y \in \mathsf{toList}\,x}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Graph model application
nodes.statement: The \emph{application} ${-} \cdot {-} : \pow{A} \times \pow{A} \to \pow{A}$ is defined by \begin{equation*} S \cdot T = \set{x \in A \such \some{y \in A} \mathsf{toSet}\,y \subseteq T \land \pair{x,y} \in S}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Application on subsets: $S\cdot T$ collects $x$ with some finite $y \subseteq T$ and $\langle x,y\rangle \in S$.
nodes.label: def:graph-model-application

nodes.name: Graph model is a combinatory algebra
nodes.statement: The set $\pow{A}$ with the application as above is a combinatory algebra.
assumptions: The set $\pow{A}$ with the application as above
nodes.label: thm:graph-model
